name: Inverted Wide 4-4-2

slots.why: The goalkeeper distributes simply into a compact defensive shape.
The defensive full-back stays behind the defensive winger to keep one flank secure.
The central defender protects the box; Cover is available for a faster player.
The ball-playing defender can switch the counter toward the open right flank.
The attacking wing-back overlaps after the inverted winger moves inside.
The defensive winger forms a protective unit with the left-back and prevents both flanks from being exposed.
The holding midfielder covers the attacking wing-back and protects central transitions.
The box-to-box midfielder carries support into the counter.
The inverted winger attacks the inside channel, creating the outside lane for the wing-back.
The deep-lying forward connects the break and releases the runner.
The advanced forward runs into the space opened by the inverted right side.

description: A 4-4-2 with a defensive winger securing one side and an inverted winger plus attacking wing-back creating a counter-attacking overload on the other.
whyGood: It gives a flat inverted winger a clear overlapping partner without asking both wide players to abandon defensive work.
whyThisShape: The left flank protects the block, while the right creates a three-player attack: the inverted winger comes inside, the wing-back overlaps and the box-to-box midfielder supports. The two strikers give each counter a link and a runner.
whenToUse: When you have a natural flat inverted winger, an energetic attacking full-back and a wide defensive specialist on the opposite side.
whenNotToUse: Against an opponent that can repeatedly isolate the attacking right-back, or when the defensive winger cannot carry his side's defensive load.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: The wing-back and defensive winger maintain useful width despite the inverted role.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Moves the ball to the forwards and right-sided overload quickly.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Finds the advanced forward and wing-back beyond the opponent's line.
instructionRationale.Overlap Right: Makes the intended outside run explicit after the inverted winger moves infield.
instructionRationale.Counter: Uses the striker pair and right-side runners immediately after a regain.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Restores the left-side defensive unit before the next transition.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Keeps the block compact without overcommitting the asymmetric flank.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Leaves cover behind the wing-back while retaining a conventional defensive line.
